transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep having these nights where I eat way more than feels normal. I’ll start with leftovers after grading papers, and then it turns into cereal, crackers, peanut butter—whatever snacks I packed for my classroom. By the end, it scares me how much I’ve eaten.
When these eating episodes happen, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?

Yes. Once I start, it’s like the sensible part of me is standing outside watching and telling me, “Joan, stop,” but I just keep opening things and eating. I don’t seem able to stop until I’m painfully full.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
I’m not sure what you mean—like, right after I eat?
After you eat like that, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to get rid of the food?
I… I don’t know. I haven’t really thought about it that way.
After you eat like that, have you ever made yourself throw up?
I’m… honestly not sure. I haven’t really thought about making myself throw up after.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to undo the calories?
Yeah. The next day I’ll skip breakfast and lunch at school, and then I’ll go hiking for hours or do extra yoga. Even if I’m shaky and exhausted, I feel like I’m supposed to keep going.
Are you currently at a very low body weight for your height?
I’m not sure what counts as very low for my height. I haven’t really looked at it that way.
After these eating episodes, have you ever made yourself throw up?
No, I don’t think I’ve ever made myself throw up after eating.
After you eat this way, do you ever use laxatives, diuretics, or diet pills to try to get rid of the calories?
I’m not really sure what all counts as those. I haven’t noticed myself doing anything like that, I don’t think.
About how often do these overeating episodes happen?
For the past few months, it’s been at least one night most weeks. I’ll eat a lot more than I planned to.
After these eating episodes, do you usually skip meals or exercise extra to make up for what you ate?
Yeah. The next day I’ll tell myself I’m not allowed to have breakfast or lunch at school. And I’ll go out on the trail for hours or do extra yoga, even if I’m shaky and exhausted.
Does your body weight or shape have a big effect on how you feel about yourself as a person?

Yeah, it really does. If my stomach looks even a little softer, or my pants feel tight before a staff meeting, I just feel like I’ve failed at everything. It doesn’t seem to matter how well prepared I am or how my students are doing.
During one of these episodes, do you eat an amount of food that most people would consider unusually large for a short period of time?

Yes. I’ll start with leftovers after grading papers, and then it turns into cereal, crackers, peanut butter, and even the snacks I packed for my classroom. It feels like way more food than I meant to eat, in a short time.
Do these overeating episodes followed by skipping meals or extra exercise happen at least once a week?

Yeah. For the past few months, I can’t really think of a week where it hasn’t happened at least once—usually one night where I eat much more than I planned, and then the next day I skip food at school or push myself into a long walk or extra yoga.
Have there been times when your weight was much lower than what would be expected for your height?
I’m not really sure what would count as much lower than expected. I haven’t been told that my weight was unusually low.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?

Yes, a lot. My evenings and weekends end up feeling like they’re all about trying to undo what happened with food. I’m slower getting grading done, I’m less present with friends, and at work I’m constantly worried about looking like I have everything together.
What is your current height and weight?
I’m not sure of my exact weight right now, and I don’t know my height off the top of my head either.
Has a doctor or anyone close to you ever told you that you were underweight?
No, not that I can remember. No one’s said I was underweight.
Have you ever skipped meals on purpose the day after eating like that to make up for the calories?
Yes. The next day I’ll tell myself I’m not allowed to have breakfast or lunch at school. Then I’ll go out on the trail for hours or do extra yoga, even if I’m shaky and exhausted.
At any time in your life, has your weight dropped so low that a doctor or other person considered you underweight for your height?
I don’t think so. I’ve never had anyone tell me my weight was too low for my height.
